what_happened: In job 8ra0, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The reading kept the earlier correction: at the start of verification, open or update the job's pull request so the CI run is a pull_request run. It did not say what to do when origin is missing or is not a GitHub remote, as in the CLI test fixtures. The user decided that case: skip the early pull request silently, with no warning line. Only a real host error on a GitHub remote prints a warning. The rest of the earlier correction stands, and merging stays with athena land.
cause: The reading stage works from the request text and has no step that asks what the environment looks like where a new action runs. It does not ask what happens when the thing the action needs, here a GitHub origin, is absent or of another kind. The CLI test fixtures have no GitHub origin, and that is a normal input shape. Nothing lists the environments an action must handle (no remote, non-GitHub remote, host error) or says which of them should be silent and which should warn. So the user supplied the no-remote and non-GitHub rules after the reading was built. The same gap produced the earlier cache-scope corrections on this job family: the reading does not model what the runtime can see.
prevention: Add a required step to the reading stage for any new action that calls an external host or depends on repo configuration. The reading must list the environment cases the action can meet: no origin, a non-GitHub origin, a GitHub origin with a host error, and a GitHub origin that works. For each case it must state the behavior (skip silently, warn, or fail) and give a test. The test fixtures' shape (no GitHub origin) must be among the cases. The list of cases would live in a checklist that the reading and the critic both consult.
proposed_request: At the start of verification, open or update the job's pull request with the candidate as its head, through the same host seam `athena land` uses, so the CI run that saves the fingerprint cache entry is a pull_request run in the pull request's scope. Opening the pull request must not merge anything; merging stays with `athena land`. When origin is missing or is not a GitHub remote (as in the CLI test fixtures), skip this step silently with no warning line. When origin is a GitHub remote and the host returns an error, print one warning line and carry on; this failure is never fatal to verification. Add tests for each case: no origin, a non-GitHub origin, a GitHub origin with a host error, and a GitHub origin that works. Each test should check that nothing is merged and that the warning appears only in the host-error case.
